standard.title: Manipulating Formulas with Digital Tools
standard.description: manipulate formulas involving several variables using digital tools, and describe the effect of systematic variation in the values of the variables
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can substitute values into formulas and generate tables of values (from AC9M7A01, AC9M7A05). Students have used digital tools for calculation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use digital tools to systematically vary values in multi-variable formulas, and describe the effect of each variable's change on the output.

nodes.label: Systematic variation of one variable
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students vary one variable in a formula while holding others constant, and describe the effect on the output.
nodes.minimum_width: Using a spreadsheet or table, vary one variable in a simple formula (e.g. V = l × w × h, vary h) and describe the effect on V.
nodes.typical_width: Systematically vary each variable in turn in a multi-variable formula; describe the relationship between each variable and the output.
wider: Investigate formulas where the output changes non-linearly with one variable (e.g. area of a square vs side length) — describe the difference.
Use spreadsheet formula functions to automate systematic variation across a range of values.

response_modes.reason: Systematic variation requires the explicit strategy of holding all variables constant except one. Students without this scaffold vary multiple things simultaneously and cannot isolate the effect of each variable.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who vary multiple variables simultaneously in Node 1 cannot describe the effect of any single variable — this blocks Node 2, where comparing the effect of different variables requires having isolated each one first.
success_criteria: Correctly varies one variable while holding others constant.
Describes the effect of the variation on the output in words.
Uses a table or digital tool to organise the systematic variation.

nodes.label: Describing effects of variation across multiple variables
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students describe how changing each variable in a multi-variable formula affects the output, and identify which variables have the greatest effect.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare the effect of equal proportional changes in two different variables on the output of a formula.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse a real formula (e.g. distance = speed × time; volume of a prism) and describe which variable has the most/least impact on the output for a given change.
wider: Explore parameter variation in formulas used in machine learning or AI contexts (as described in elaborations) — model the concept of tuning parameters.
Investigate the formula for compound scenarios: if both speed and time double, what happens to distance? Connect to proportional reasoning.

response_modes.reason: Comparing the effect of variables requires varied formula contexts to develop generalised understanding. Students who only explore one formula see the pattern as context-specific rather than a feature of multi-variable relationships.

success_criteria: Correctly describes the effect of changing each variable on the output.
Identifies which variable produces the largest change in output for an equal proportional variation.
Uses digital tool output systematically rather than performing isolated calculations.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Parameter variation in multi-variable formulas is the conceptual foundation for modelling and AI — advancing students can investigate compound variation and connect to proportional reasoning in ways that go well beyond the minimum.
